correctness.rationale: For an odd extraspecial group, any idempotent with nonabelian image has trivial kernel and is the identity; a proper retract must kill the center, be elementary abelian and project onto an isotropic subspace in the kernel of the p-power linear functional. Conversely every permitted isotropic r-subspace admits exactly p^r complementary lifts and each lift admits exactly p^(r(2n-r)) retractions. The symplectic and hyperplane isotropic counts yield the stated complete formulas. Generator-image exhaustive checks of the two groups of order p³ for p=3,5 and independent symplectic rank-2 subspace counts for p=3,5 replay the critical cases; finite checks are not used as general proof.

evidence: arXiv:1908.00331v2 §5 Theorem 5.2 gives alpha_r and beta_r isotropic-subspace counts, while Theorem 5.3 counts all endomorphisms through numbers gamma_r of all surjective maps.

The paper includes no idempotency condition and no condition that maps restrict to identity on their images. Those conditions replace unrestricted surjections by projections and require treatment of central lifts.

The new proof shows that every proper retract is an elementary abelian complement to Z and that each isotropic r-space yields exactly p^(r(2n-r+1)) endomorphisms; these multiplicities are not the source gamma_r counts.

originality.rationale: The complete 2019 primary full-text HTML was inspected at the main classification theorems and Section 5. It provides total-endomorphism descriptions and isotropic-space counts, but not idempotent or retract enumerations. Separate scientific-record and public literature searches for retractions, idempotent endomorphism monoids, symplectic projection versions and exact count fingerprints found no covering statement. The proof isolates an intrinsic semigroup invariant by classifying splittings and computing their multiplicities; the reliance on source isotropic counts is explicit.
residual_risks: An older group-theoretic classification of retracts under semidirect decompositions might imply these profiles without using the phrase idempotent endomorphism.
The source endomorphism formulas and its isotropic-subspace enumeration are strong inputs; the new count is a refinement rather than an unrelated new classification.
Database absence and failed literature searches cannot certify absolute novelty.

value.rationale: Idempotents in an endomorphism monoid classify actual group retracts, hence reveal its splitting structure rather than just its cardinality. The theorem classifies every proper retract and exactly counts retraction multiplicities for both isomorphism types in every rank and odd characteristic; rank-one counts differ by the clean exponent-sensitive quantity p^(4n-1). This is a natural, full semigroup invariant in the family explicitly studied for total endomorphisms by the source, not a routine fixed small example or an arbitrary parameter slice.
